title: Statistics Fundamentals
intro: Statistics is a core part of the SAT Problem-Solving and Data Analysis domain. This chapter covers the measures of center and spread — mean, median, mode, range, quartiles and the interquartile range. Read each topic, try the problems with the hint ladder, then take the 8-question topic test.

items.name: Mean
items.formula: sum of values ÷ number of values

items.name: Median
items.formula: middle value of the ordered list

items.name: Q1, Q3
items.formula: medians of the lower and upper halves

topics.name: Mean
topics.details: The mean (average) is the sum of all the values divided by how many there are. It balances the data and is sensitive to every value, so a single very large or very small number can pull it noticeably. Useful rearrangements appear often on the SAT: the sum equals mean × count, so if you know the average and the number of values you can recover the total, or find a missing value. Adding a new value equal to the current mean leaves the mean unchanged. Recognising "average = total ÷ count" in both directions is the key skill.

solved.solution: Sum = 36; divide by 4: mean = 9.

solved.problem: The mean of 5 numbers is 12. What is their sum?
solved.solution: Sum = mean × count = 12 × 5 = 60.

solved.problem: Four tests average 80. A fifth score of 90 is added. New mean?
solved.solution: Total = 320 + 90 = 410; divide by 5 = 82.

solved.problem: The mean of 3, 7, x is 6. Find x.
solved.solution: Sum must be 18; 3 + 7 + x = 18, so x = 8.

unsolved.problem: The mean of 6 numbers is 15. What is their sum?
The mean of 4, 8, x is 7. Find x.
Five numbers average 20. One more, equal to 20, is added. New mean?
hints: Adding a value equal to the mean.

unsolved.problem: Three numbers have mean 10; two of them are 8 and 9. Find the third.

topics.name: Median
topics.details: The median is the middle value once the data is put in order. For an odd number of values it is the single middle one; for an even number it is the mean of the two middle values. Because it depends only on position, the median is resistant to outliers — extreme values barely move it, unlike the mean. Always sort first; forgetting to order the list is the classic error. On the SAT the median is favoured for skewed data, and questions often compare how the mean and median respond to an extreme value.

solved.solution: Sorted: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; the middle value is 3.
Even count: mean of the two middle values (4 and 6) = 5.
Sorted: 2,4,6,8,10,12; middle two are 6 and 8; median = 7.

solved.problem: A set of 9 numbers has median 15. The largest is increased. New median?
solved.solution: The middle position is unchanged, so the median stays 15.

hints: Average the two middle values (8 and 10).

unsolved.problem: A set of 7 numbers has median 20. The smallest decreases. New median?
hints: Order of the middle value is unchanged.

topics.name: Mode
topics.details: The mode is the value that appears most often in a data set. A set can have one mode, more than one (if several values tie for most frequent), or no mode at all (if every value occurs once). The mode is the only measure of center that works for non-numerical data, such as the most common colour or response. It is unaffected by outliers. On the SAT the mode appears in frequency tables and "which value occurs most" questions; the main skill is counting occurrences carefully and recognising when there is a tie or no mode.

solved.solution: 3 occurs most often, so the mode is 3.
4 and 6 each occur twice — two modes (bimodal).
Every value occurs once, so there is no mode.
5 occurs three times, the most, so the mode is 5.

topics.name: Range
topics.details: The range measures spread as the difference between the largest and smallest values: range = maximum − minimum. It is quick to compute but uses only the two extremes, so it is very sensitive to outliers and ignores everything in between. A small range means the data is tightly clustered; a large range means it is spread out. On the SAT, range questions test careful identification of the max and min (after any change to the data) and contrast with the interquartile range, which is more robust to extreme values.

solved.solution: Max 9, min 2; range = 9 − 2 = 7.
Max 20, min 11; range = 9.

solved.problem: A set has range 50. The smallest is increased by 10 and the largest decreased by 10. New range?

solved.solution: Max and min are both 6; range = 0.

unsolved.problem: A set has range 30. The largest decreases by 5. New range?
hints: Lowering the max reduces the range.

topics.name: Quartiles
topics.details: Quartiles split ordered data into four equal parts. The second quartile (Q2) is the median. The first quartile (Q1) is the median of the lower half, and the third quartile (Q3) is the median of the upper half. When the data has an odd count, the overall median is excluded from both halves before finding Q1 and Q3. About 25% of the data lies below Q1 and 75% below Q3. Quartiles underlie box plots and the interquartile range. On the SAT, the main skills are ordering the data and correctly splitting it into halves.

solved.solution: Lower half is 2, 4, 6; its median is 4, so Q1 = 4.
Upper half is 8, 10, 12; its median is 10, so Q3 = 10.
The middle value is 5.
Lower half 1,2,3,4; median = (2 + 3)/2 = 2.5.

topics.name: Interquartile Range
topics.details: The interquartile range (IQR) is the spread of the middle 50% of the data: IQR = Q3 − Q1. Because it ignores the extreme quarters, the IQR is resistant to outliers and is the preferred measure of spread for skewed data — unlike the range, which the extremes dominate. A common SAT use is comparing the consistency of two data sets: the one with the smaller IQR is more tightly clustered in the middle. The IQR is also used to flag outliers. The skill is finding Q1 and Q3 correctly, then subtracting.

solved.problem: Given Q1 = 10 and Q3 = 20, find the IQR.
A data set has Q1 = 15 and Q3 = 35. IQR?
Which is more consistent: IQR 5 or IQR 12?
solved.solution: A smaller IQR means tighter spread, so the set with IQR 5.

unsolved.problem: Given Q1 = 8 and Q3 = 23, find the IQR.
A data set has Q1 = 20 and Q3 = 50. IQR?
Which data set is more spread out: IQR 4 or IQR 11?
